improvement_notes: Add one brief, authentic ROS 2 command-line demonstration, such as `ros2 topic list`, `ros2 topic echo`, or `ros2 topic info`, so students connect the structural Python model to the actual platform named throughout the lesson.

Reduce repetition around topic contracts, invalid data, stale messages, and the limitations of the Python model. The cautions are valuable, but several appear in multiple sections and lengthen a foundational lesson.
Clarify that ROS 2 publisher/subscriber matching requires compatible topic names, interface types, and QoS compatibility, while QoS settings are not necessarily identical between endpoints.
The `diagram.png` section is followed by prose describing what an illustrator could draw, even though the visual already exists. Replace that paragraph with a direct visual-reading task or remove it.
The worked example could include one deliberately delayed or missing message in its table so the freshness and timeout discussion becomes experimentally testable rather than primarily explanatory.

The optional WarningNode challenge would be stronger with a small expected implementation outline or a stated callback behavior, allowing beginners to focus on topic routing rather than infer all architecture decisions independently.
